After a bit of short research, I have come to the conclusion that the reason Anawrahta has become so well-known was because of the contributions to the spread of Buddhism he made, along with his successful attempt at unifying the general lands of Myanmar, the standardization of Theravada Buddhism, and finally the building of multiple Buddhist structures like the Pagoda.

After some much deeper research, I have realized the history of the Bagan had levels to it. Apparently, after the mysterious death of King Anawrahta, King Saw Lu, the heir of King Anawrahta, ascended to the throne, even though he was quite an inexperienced and unskilled king. It likely should've been Kyansittha that should've inherited the throne, but he was discarded and exiled by King Anawrata for having an affair with Manisanda. He was eventually brought back at the urging of the Primate Shin Arahan, although he was soon exiled once more for his renewed with Manisanda. Although multiple chronicles regarding the exact events do not agree with each other at all, what seems most agreed on is that it was after a game of dice where Yamankan, a childhood friend appointed for the Won-speaking territories, won, that Saw Lu taunted him to rebel if he was so clever. Aware of the weak leadership skills of Saw Lu, Yamankan did so, somewhere around the early 1080s. The weak leadership of Saw Lu led to their losses and the eventual death of Saw Lu, and this led to the appointment of King Kyansittha, who, today, is regarded as one of the greatest monarchs of the First Burmese Empire. He was eventually able to repair the damage caused by the turmoil of Saw Lu's death, and continue Anawrahta's mission, with Myanmar becoming a more internationally and culturally recognized state toward the end of his reign, proving his leadership effective in the long run. As a side note, the predicament of King Saw Lu was what proved the power of Anawrahta's leadership that prevented bigger problems from forming, that could've caused the fall of the continuous First Burmese Empire before it grew past its infancy.
